summary: CKGSB's marketing push is now centred on Asia Star and Intelligent China as the top two priorities, with the knowledge website redesign and SEO/AI-search visibility in active development, while a cluster of partnership and content deadlines hits this week.
summaryDetail: The big strategic shift is clear: Asia Star and the new Intelligent China program are now the team's top two marketing priorities, with US programs (Stanford, Columbia, Berkeley) deprioritised and partnership programs on hold to concentrate on China. Supporting that push, the knowledge website redesign is at a decision point — the two-menu structure and BCI banner placement are settled, but the team still needs a 30-minute feedback session to mark up the design concepts before Joker makes further changes, and Joseph must share the inspirational HTML file. This week's urgent items are a mix of partnership and content deadlines: Kaylee must send the prepared SwissCham email on the 2026 Sino-Swiss Economic Forum (CKGSB is participating as a free Knowledge Partner), Julie must finalise the MBA new-intake social post (removing the 247 figure and sourcing a ceremony photo), and Xuan should meet Graeme Wallace at the Beijing campus to discuss the Nov 13 Shanghai event. On the SEO/AI-search front, Joseph needs to get the conversion-tracking brief from the SEO manager and the team must audit the setup, while Joseph also drafts the target areas/prompts and audience focus document and the team analyses Asia Star participant profiles and CRM hot leads. Looking ahead, the European Chamber Silver Economy Series II event on Oct 29 needs an attendee, Cathy should share recently completed English case studies, and the approved brand video timeline is now in motion.
